Sensory Tri-View · the offenders you ruled on and your side note on the sun, before and now (16 November 2026)

One bullet per offender, numbered as in your rulings, then your side note on the sun. Every picture is the True-Person view from the held shoulder camera unless it says otherwise, with the state you saw before beside the scene as it stands now. Seconds are the video player's.

You passed all of it on 16 November. The page is brought up to the scene as it stands: with your side note the sunrise moved to where the script always meant it, so every picture after the crest (player 50 s) now shows the room in sunlight, and the sun that stood in his head before it had risen is gone from the pictures of the doze.

Stand-ins in every picture: the simulated mannequin and its motion (rung 3), the timeline's timings (rung 4), the room, the trees, the bushes, the lamps and the light (rung 5), and the scans at 1024 where the piece will use 2048. What lasts is the rule each bullet names.

  • 1The remembered window: its sill and its side are whole

    What you are seeing

    From the bed his eyes see the top of the sill and the side of the window almost edge-on, so the picture holds only a few rows of them, with gaps between the rows. The outside showed through the gaps as white wedges. The picture he sees with his eyes open closes such gaps with the thing's known shape. The remembered picture now does the same for flat-faced things.

  • 5The remembered sun is a ball again
    His eyes shut in the sun, player 105.3 s. The sun enlarged four times.
    What you are seeing
    Left, the remembered sun in the state you ruled on. Middle and right, now, at two moments 1.3 s apart.
    New, to pass off on
    A grey ball, opaque as every memory is, with the ripple's soft light and dark across it. It shimmers as the bushes do and stays a ball. At four times enlargement its outline is lumpy and, at the moment in the middle panel, a crease crosses it: that is the ripple itself, the same that bends the bushes. The clip sent with this page shows it moving.
    Check it has not changed
    The bushes and trees still shimmer as you passed them. The one rule added here trims only the largest movements of the smallest bushes.
    Why it happened
    Two causes. First: with his eyes shut the remembered sky is drawn a hair nearer than the sky he sees, and the sun ball was left where it was, so the remembered sky cut through the ball and only a sliver of it showed. The ball now moves with the remembered picture. Second, you were right that the sun's shimmer was stronger: I measured it. The ripple's waves are four times wider than tall. A bush is low and wide, so the waves barely bend it. The sun is as tall as it is wide and smaller than a wave, so it was sheared by a quarter of its size, twice as much as a bush as wide.
    The rule added
    No remembered thing that the mind holds whole is bent by its ripple by more than 15% of its own size. It applies to every such thing. The big bushes were already under it.
    Lasting or stand-in
    Both rules last. The sun ball's size and the bushes are stand-ins.

Your side note on the sun

Both things you asked me to check were wrong in the scene, and both are fixed. Three more faults turned up at the same moment.

  • S1The sun is not in his head before it reaches his eyes
    The doze, player 31.3 to 31.6 s.
    What you are seeing
    Top: what his eyes see (First-Person), then the model in his head at the same moment, before and now. Bottom: the same with his eyes shut.
    What was wrong
    From player 27.1 s the model drew the sun in the window as seen, and through the doze it stood as a memory, though it was still behind the range.
    Why it happened
    The engine's lines of sight toward the sun stopped 200 m out. The stand-in range is 300 m away, so it never hid the sun from his mind. They now reach past whatever stands before the sun.
    Now
    Nothing of the sun is in his head until player 50.25 s, the frame its edge clears the range from where his eyes are. From that frame the model shows the sun whole and at full strength: a sliver dazzles as the whole does.
    Lasting or stand-in
    The rule lasts. The range and the sun's size in the model are stand-ins.
  • S2His hand against the sun is a reaction to the light
    The crest, player 49.7 to 52.3 s. A timeline, before and now.
    What was wrong
    In the scene as built, the range hid the sun from where he sits until player 66.2 s. His lids, head and hand all started at 50.25 s, the second the script called first light. He blocked a light that was sixteen seconds away.
    Now
    The sunlight comes down the wall behind him from 49.8 s and reaches his open eyes at 50.25 s. His lids begin to shut 0.16 s later, his head flinches 0.19 s later, and his hand starts 0.31 s later and takes 0.79 s to come between his eyes and the sun.
    How it is kept true
    Every build measures, in the scene itself, the frame the light first reaches his open eyes, prints it beside the script's number, and warns if he moves first.
    Lasting or stand-in
    The check lasts. The motion and its reaction times are stand-ins (rungs 3 and 4). In the concept he takes two breaths before lifting his head; the stand-in motion answers at once.
